utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Your affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply. Can I mention that if there is a need for a speedy adjournment, the accused should simply make that known quickly and that can be arranged. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I forget. Yesterday the last document that we looked at was from 65 ter 2D00-713, from the NATO handbook of 2001. That NATO handbook is actually 536 pages long. I do not propose to burden the Chamber with the entire work. However, I would seek to tender page 1 the title page and pages 42 to 47 which is the chapter that is referred to in the expert report of Dr. Markovski at note 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P00603. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, do you have a copy of your report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if Dr. Markovski could also be provided with the first Prosecution binder as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Doctor, if we can turn, please, to paragraph -- I believe it's 51 of your report. Actually, I misspoke, paragraph 52, please. And at the bottom of paragraph 52, Doctor, we see the following sentence: That is why it was no coincidence that the crisis in Macedonia began in Tanusevci that it was immediately subsequent to the signing of the border agreement with Macedonia's northern neighbour and that occurred at the time when the Yugoslav army, with permission from KFOR, entered the buffer zone in southern Serbia and squeezed out the armed extremists of the so-called LAPMB. And then as authority for that comment, you have footnote 25 than is document from the Ministry of Interior than is 65 ter 2D526, and that is at tab 25 of binder number 1, and should be there, both in English and in Macedonian, Doctor. And as you can see, this document is from the Ministry of Interior, security and counter-intelligence administration, dated the 11th of March, 2001, and the title is: "Operative intelligence points to a possible deterioration of the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the first paragraph tell us that the UBK's recent operative intelligence points to the possible spread of the activities of the armed terrorist groups in the north-western part of Macedonia and also indicates that they intend to undertake terrorist attacks in Skopje, Tetovo, Kicevo, and Struga. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you move down to the fifth paragraph starting with the name Beqir Sinani, it says -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it on the same page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, it's on the next page. If you turn to the next page. Do you see the word -- the name Beqir Sinani?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Sinani Beqir, can I see that, yes, from Malino.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see from that paragraph that Mr. Sinani plays a significant role in supplying the terrorists with weapons and recruiting volunteers for the NLA who operate in the area of Tanusevci, Brest, Malino. And then we're told that Sinani receives his instructions in connection with the procurement of distribution of weapons from Ali Ahmeti, who is referred to as in parenthesis a functionary of the national movement for the liberation of Kosovo, or the NDK. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph, we're told that --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, because there is a parenthesis, a high official of the NDK we have to say that he was one of the founders of the NLA and a direct participant of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry the interpreters did not catch the very last word that you said. Just the last Word?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. You said that he was a high official of the KLA, and we have a parenthesis and it says that he was the founder of the KLA and a direct participant in the liberation army of Presevo and Medvedje; so he was all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The next paragraph, we're told that, according to the UBK's intelligence Xhemal Hiseini, (one of the NLA commanders) has been assisted by Murat Jashari (a member of the NDK leadership) and particular members of the LAPMB, originally from the Kumanovo area in intensively collecting financial means and carrying out the transport of weapons and medicines for the needs of the NLA. Did you follow with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then just below that, we see a sentence a large quantity of food and uniforms for the needs of the NLA has allegedly been stockpiled in the school in Tanusevci. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: This intelligence report tell us about commanders collecting money and transporting weapons and medicine for the NLA and it tells -- it talks about the storing or stockpiling of food and uniforms for the NLA.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I don't see anywhere commanders and "komandants."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Go to the paragraph beginning with: "According to the UBK's intelligence ..." Do you see that paragraph. We read it a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is just one of the commanders of the LAPMB. Ali Ahmeti, it doesn't say about Sinan Beqiri, Hiseini.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, if you just listen to my questions, then I think we could move through this more quickly.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The reference to Xhemal Hiseini says in parentheses one of the NLA commanders. So my question is simply this, we have intelligence information here about commanders of the NLA, collecting money and transporting weapons and medicine for the needs of the NLA, food and uniforms being stockpiled in large quantities for the NLA. Doesn't this illustrate a fair amount of organisational capability on the part of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all, my intervention was quite all right. I was correct when I said this. We don't see this, what you are saying. We see certain names, certain individuals that have been named, and just for one person, it is listed and says one of the NLA commanders, than is why I cannot accept the fact that all these peoples were commanders and they all managed other people, especially bearing in mind the person Ali Ahmeti, because it reads that at the same time he was an official of the NDK, founder of the NLA or KLA, and participant in the LAPMB. You will agree with me also that I cannot be both same time in The Hague and Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, what did you mean by that last comment?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to say that these individuals can not sit on two separate chairs at the same time, so they are either people who collect and distribute, or they are commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you see, I didn't say that all of these people were commanders. I was simply reading from the document, and in one paragraph of the document there's a description of Xhemal Hiseini as one of the KLA commanders, that's all. Neither myself nor the document is saying that every individual mentioned is a commander. So one more time. Doesn't the fact that people are collecting money, transporting weapons and medicine, storing feed and uniforms in large quantities for the needs of the NLA, doesn't that suggest a large organisational compatibility?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know on what you base this -- this assertion of yours. This is a group of four to five people who did that, and there is no suggestion that this is an organised institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that you read this document to suggest that only the specific individuals mentioned in this document are involved in these activities? Is that how you read this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I read the document as it says, and I cannot assume what happened further on, because I don't know how everything was organised. It is obvious that these three to four people did not collect all these items, bearing them on their backs. Probably they had their own collaborators, but this is not explained here and we ask not discuss the precise number; and we cannot say it was an organised group or mercenaries. Maybe we can make even this kind of assumption, people that would do all of this for money.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on. If you take a look, please, going back to your report, Dr. Markovski, and if you could take a look at paragraph 57 of your report. Paragraph 57, the start of the paragraph says this -- actually, Your Honour, before I forget, could I tender that last document that I showed you, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean the one at tab 25?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. It was 65 ter 2D526.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be exhibit number P00604. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Doctor paragraph 57 in the beginning, says that: "The first form of terrorism occurred in 1999," describes an incident there where a soldier Mr. Krstanovski tragically lost his live and then lower down it says: "Other drastic examples of terrorist acts subsequent to this are as follows." And then you list a series of events. But at the word "follows" there is a footnote. It is footnote number 26. And as authority for this paragraph you cite to 65 ter 701?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I'm wondering whether we could show that to Dr. Markovski, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is at tab 26 of that first binder, doctor. What I see on the screen, I do not believe is 65 ter 701.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But do you have it in front of you in the hard copy, Doctor? It's a document dated 25 July 2001 and the title is: "Information on the NLA activities in the territory of Macedonia. Do you have that, okay?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And now I see it's coming up on the -- on e-court as well. This is a document from the Ministry of Interior, from the department of security and counter-intelligence. And, first of all, you relied on this document as authority for paragraph 57. So can we take it that you believe that the information in this document is reliable and correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the information is reliable, but it comes from an official body, from the state administration. And I do trust the country of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so that I understand you, you're not sure whether this document and the information it contains is reliable?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you misunderstood. I'm not a witness of these events in order to trust or not. This is a document from an official body of the Republic of Macedonia and in this regard, I do trust it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, -- and by the way, Your Honours, just to correct something. On the list of exhibits in your binders this document is at tab 26. However, the description is incorrect. Just I wanted to clarify that so as not to create confusion for Your Honours and for my colleagues. The ERN is correct but the description of the document is not correct. If we can take a look at the first paragraph in the introduction. You see a sentence a few lines down beginning with: "The armed groups." Do you see that? It's in the middle of paragraph, a sentence beginning with: "The armed groups."

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this sentence says: "The armed groups of the Albanian extremists who call themselves National Liberation Army, or NLA, by means of organised violence, are trying to effectuate certain political goals in the interests of the Albanians in Macedonia and to impose themselves as the only negotiating factor in the realisation of these goals." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does the phrase "organised violence" include organised attacks on the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, indeed, what the author meant with this thesis. However, organised violence is not limited by territory or force, for that matter, with respect to the numbers. Organised violence can be organised by two or three people on a territory of just a single village, if it was exercised in a planned manner, then one might say that it was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but you're not answering my question. My question was simple. I'll ask it again. Does the phrase "organised violence" include or would the phrase "organised violence" include organised attacks on the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is possible, but the answer is no. I have to make an emphasis here. I am afraid, Mr. Saxon, that we might be looking at the wrong document. Maybe it is just me looking at the wrong document, because the document that you pointed out of the 25th of July, 2005 does not correspond with the assertion in paragraph 57. I think the number listed is different N000-9146, 9179, that is to say, 65 ter 701, because the events that are described here, this is 2001. And in paragraph 57, I am discussing the events in 2000. I think that there might be some kind of misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, this is the document that you cited to in -- as authority in paragraph 57. So I am simply reviewing this document with you, all right? This is the document that you cited to, all right? Now --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then please help me out, because in front of me I have the document 0171938.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Footnote 26, I refer to a document N000-9164 and N000-9179. I don't know whether we are discussing the same document at all. But it is obvious that according to the dates it seems that this is not the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your footnote refers to 65 ter 701 and that is the document in front of you. Your footnote refers to a document from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, department of security and counter-intelligence. That is the document in front of you. And it refers to a document dated July 25th, 2001, which is this document. And the problem -- I can simplify the problem, Dr. Markovski. Your footnote refers to the English version. Dr. Markovski, look. Look, Dr. Markovski. My version, the English version, has the number that is in the footnote, all right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I don't blame you that you gave me the wrong document. I just blame myself that I was not looking at the right document. We are discussing certain events, but this document discusses events from 2001, so maybe it's my bed. I'm just trying to reach the right document discussing the events from 2000, and I'm quite convinced that the basis of my report was maybe another document that described the events that are referred in this paragraph; and you can also conclude that there is a discrepancy between the period that I discussion and the period you are talking to me about in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That may be, Dr. Markovski, but there is the document that you referred to in your report as authority in this paragraph. So I simply want to discuss this document with you, all right? Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely we are going to agree. There is no dilemma. I just wanted to say that my paragraph refers to events in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that before. You don't have to repeat it again. A minute ago, I asked you whether the phrase "organised violence" could include attacks on the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. And you responded: No, it is possible, but the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say the answer is no, but it is possible, but the basic answer was no. So there are possibilities for something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if you go to -- if we turn to the bottom of page 4 in the English version, and this will be page 5 in your version, in the Macedonian version, Dr. Markovski. We'll see a subsection entitled: The National Liberation Army, NLA, and then the word "goals." Do you see that? The fifth page of your version.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my printed version, in the folder. Now I see it on the screen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now, in the very first paragraph of that subsection, in the second sentence it says this: "The aim of this terrorist organisation is to change the constitution of Macedonia and endanger the security in the country by applying organised violence, and by doing so to occupy Macedonian territories?" Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I don't see it. Can you point out precisely where you read this from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the phrase: "The National Liberation Army." Look at the hard copy in front of you.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the word "goals" beneath it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I tell you, yes, I see the title: Goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the -- the second sentence: "The aim of this terrorist organisation ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, can you look at your hard copy, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, but in the Macedonian version, it says: Purposes and maybe that is why the witness was confused and the second sentence does not begin with the word purpose or goals. This is not how the sentence beginning in the Macedonian version. That is maybe why we have this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to read the second sentence to you, Dr. Markovski and hopefully what I read to you will look like what you see in your language, all right. "The aim of this terrorist organisation," aim and purpose can be synonymous in English, "is to change the constitution of Macedonia and endanger the security in the country by applying organised violence and by doing so to occupy Macedonian territories." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is now proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, isn't that what happened in 2001? Isn't that what the NLA eventually accomplished?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: NLA did not manage to achieve anything. The crisis in 2001, unfortunately, and for Macedonian misfortune, turned Macedonia at least ten years backwards in every sense of the word, in both economic and political, and any other aspect and cultural aspect. So all of us in the Republic of Macedonia lost. However, a result of everything that took place and which was the product of the plan of the President Trajkovski to eliminate, the threat to deal with the crisis that is, was strongly supported and aided by the international institutions represented in the Republic of Macedonia, and together with the relevant political entities, the political Ohrid Agreement was adopted which significantly changes the structure and the position of the Republic of Macedonia as a state. On the other hand, I wish to indicate that the attempts to resolve certain issues that became problems in the societal life in the Republic of Macedonia emerged as early as 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But interrupted in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there and I'm ask you from now on to give brief answers to my questions. Well, it's true, isn't it then that what the NLA set out to do in 2001 eventually occurred, didn't it? Territory --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The answer is an emphatic no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If you go to the next page in the -- in the English version, page 5, and page 6 in the Macedonian version, please, Doctor, there is a subheading there called methods. Do you see it? Can you look at it please on the hard copy that is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that section says: "The NLA applies terrorist methods. They are trying to fulfil their goals by causing explosions, fire, and other dangerous activities and acts of organised violence in order to create fear and instability among the citizens of Macedonia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, please, some video material.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but, again, you had a foresight here because you again placed this quote outside of its natural context. You did not add that the aim of the NLA was to destroy the constitutional order of the Republic of Macedonia and to endanger its security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, I'd like to you let me ask the questions and you to just answer them, all right. The Chamber can see what is written in that paragraph, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I am able to assist, the English translation of the Macedonian text is wrong so this might what creates the confusion. It should be the constitutional order and not the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. In the Macedonian text, it readings: Constitutional order, not the constitution of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, carry on, please, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please see what will be 65 ter 1120.5. This is a video with ERN VOOO-7474, it's clip 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is more material from MRTV, Dr. Markovski. It's from the 11th of August, 2001, and it talks about the situation in Radusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can start that clip, please. It's the wrong clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop it there. Can we stop it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see by 52 seconds that at the moment in the Radusa region there are terrorist actions with small arms, machine-guns and mortar weapons, but at the same time that the army and police forces in this area, under the unified command are acting forcefully?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move forward now, please, to about 4 minutes. Right there, if we can start there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop please. Can we move back to about 3:30. Okay, right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there. We see at 3:46 we're told that terrorists together with the groups of the Kosovo Protection Corps have been attacking the Macedonian security forces and where there is still heavy fighting and then we see the -- the commentary is turned over to another journalist. Can we start again, please. Can we now go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there. We see homes burning in the village at 4:35.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see homes burning at 4:35, we saw a few seconds before this a combat helicopter. Can we start again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there, please. At 4:42 we see the helicopter firing what appear to be rockets. Can we go again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please. We've seen enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, what we just saw from the 11th of August, 2001, wouldn't that be an act of organised violence?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we have here is the 11th of August, 2001, some information are accurate, some presented here by the journalists are not. I remember this event well, since I was at the -- at the time at the position when it was necessary for me to follow the events. There was a police station there, and the internal --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Dr. Markovski, a simple yes or no would do. What we just saw on this video from the 11th of August, did we see just an act of organised violence?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that it will be difficult for the two of us to understand one another, Mr. Saxon, but the picture is never black or white. What you are asking me can't really satisfy the needs of your question. What I can tell you is that this is armed violence, this is violence, but this is not a sufficient answer that would depict the situation here precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, armed violence at this level would require a certain degree of organisation, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this video-clip, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be exhibit number P00605. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yesterday at page 10756 of the transcript, Dr. Markovski, I asked you whether during 2001 the security forces lived and worked in a situation of combat and you replied: "No, no, that would be too harsh an assertion, which is not based in reality." Doctor, doesn't the video that we just saw from Radusa in 2001 illustrate a combat situation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Today it seems that I'm inclined to oppose you all the time. You did not cite to my full answer. I said that they lived in a state of increased combat readiness. I am a bit old man, but I do remember what I have said. So please ask the question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know that's what you said, Doctor, and after you said that, I asked you the following: "Didn't the security forces live and work in a situation of combat?" You replied, page 10756 of the transcript: "No, no that is correct would be too harsh an assertion, which is not based in reality." Now, my question was: Doesn't the video that we just saw of Radusa in August 2001 illustrate a combat situation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a terrorist attack against the police station in Radusa, and the news or their representation was not correct that the police and the army acted jointly. The terrorist attack was carried out against the police station during the time when the police makes the assessment that because of infiltration of armed extremist groups from Kosovo, there was an increased presence of armed persons at Radusa and they had insufficient forces and means to deal with these terrorist attacks, they request assistance from the army. The army was not involved until the moment, or perhaps I won't be precise but it was sometime after 1700 hours, when the police forces, in the Radusa region, were given fire support from the aviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the aviation falls within the army of the Republic of Macedonia, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aircrafts were not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, you saw a helicopter, didn't you, firing rockets a few minutes ago in the video-clip. So helicopters were used, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said fire support from the aviation to the police so that it can deal with the terrorist act carried out by the armed terrorist groups and for the police against whom there was fire from several sides, to be withdrawn, to be taken from the area. I need to mention that the police has left the police station there, which means that it was surrounded by the armed extremist Albanian groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, the helicopters that were firing rockets at the NLA member, those helicopters were under the jurisdiction of the army, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to go back for a moment to this video material, and it is now P00605. If we can go back to this same video-clip, please, the one we just saw, and before we begin, I just want to note what you told us a minute ago. "The aircrafts were not used." If we can start the video, please, and --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise. Before you begin, I said aeroplanes were not uses which means they did not act.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can we scroll to around six minutes please on this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A bit more, please. Okay, right there is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can go about 30 seconds more forward, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's a fixed wing aircraft, isn't it, Dr. Markovski. That is a fixed wing aircraft that we see coming in here, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So what you said before when you said the aircrafts were not used want quite correct, was it? This is at 7:30 of the video.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was absolutely right, and I'm still standing at that statement. The aeroplanes with regards to the events that we're discussing, did not act. Obviously they were flying, but they did not act.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay, well they were certainly prepared to act, if necessary, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macedonia is prepared to act today also, if someone attacks it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll take your response as a yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, no? I'm emphatic that they did not participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I said I would take your response as a yes, Dr. Markovski. So we agree?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that the aviation did not participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that. The question I asked you was that they were prepared to participate, and you replied: "The forces of Macedonia are always prepared." And I said: "I will take that as a yes."

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, please move on, will you, yes. We are wasting time. The Chamber can well see the effect of what is occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Can we please turn to paragraph 267 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 267, Dr. Markovski, refers to a letter that you say President Trajkovski sent on the 11th of August, to Kofi Annan, Secretary-General of the United Nations, and to George Robertson, Secretary-General of NATO. And you explain that the letter to Robertson stated that in the course of the day on 11 August 2001, the security forces and the local population in the area of the village Radusa and the village Rogacevo were exposed to continual attack from infantry and artillery fire by the terrorists? And then a few lines later goes on to say: "The security forces of the Republic of Macedonia refrained from responding to these attacks." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were refraining.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I think -- I think the meaning is the same. Well, what the president told George Robertson, then, wasn't quite true, was it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak about what the president said to Mr. Robertson and whether that was completely accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, didn't see from a video-clip that I showed you a minute ago that the security forces quite actively responded to the attacks in Radusa?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that was a reaction, because they were constantly under attack by the infantry from the villages of Radusa and village Rogacevo so that was reaction, a defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're right. So where the president said, according to you at paragraph 267, that the security forces refrained from responding to these attacks wasn't quite true, was it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like this: You could have noticed from the video-clip as well, that, actually, the penetration of the armed extremist gangs from Kosovo started in the evening on the 10th, if I understood it well, and I believe I did because I know the situation well and then the events then took place on the 11th. So up until the moment when the police station was attacked, it was obvious that the police officers present there were restraining; and this is why I don't see that there is anything illogical here, because to restrain and to be restraining, denotes two different tenses in Macedonian and it has two different meanings so they were retraining, up until the moment when their personal safety was at risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn back to what is 65 ter 701, please. This is, again, at -- in binder number 1, tab 26. And, actually, before we go back into this document,.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to go back briefly to your expert report, which is Exhibit 2D00101. If you could turn to paragraph 328, please, Doctor. Can you turn to paragraph 328.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 328.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 328 begins: "At the start of the escalation of the crisis, the activities of the terrorists amounted to assassinations and attacks on army and police officials. The attacks were carried out by smaller groups on distinct targets and significant buildings, which had the effect of sowing fear and uncertainty and prevented the officials from completing their tasks. The attacks employed weapons from distance, but the terrorist actions applied the tactic of hit and run, in cases where infantry weapons were used. There were almost no instances of lengthy clashes and casualties among the armed Albanian groups. This created the impression of untouchability and independence, in the undertaking of terrorist acts." Now, if we can move back to 65 ter 701, please, the document that you cited to in your report earlier, the information on the NLA activities in the territory of Macedonia. This document has a chronology section, and the chronology section lists a number of events that occurred during 2001. And if you could turn, please, Doctor, in the Macedonian version to the bottom of page 12 and for those following in the English, this will be page 10 in the English version. We don't seem to have a Macedonian version, but here it comes. Go to the next page in the Macedonian version, please. And starting at the bottom of page 12 in the Macedonian version and in the middle of the English page, which is page 10, we see an entry that says: "On June the 5th, 2001 at 1915 hours ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that entry begins: "Terrorists attacked the Macedonian security forces at the Sipkovica Krivena post in the Tetovo area."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we move one more page in the Macedonian version, please and move up to the top of the screen and focus on the first several paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see that it says: "The attack was conducted with grenades and automatic weapons from different directions. In addition, there was a mortar attack coming from the first houses in the village of Sipkovica-Tetovo. During the attack, five members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were killed," and it gives the names of those soldiers, and then it says that three soldiers were wounded and transferred to the military hospital in Skopje. Have you been following with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was this a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the categories, yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And which categories are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Categories or characteristics of terrorism or manifestations of terrorist activities. Let me explain. We are discussing the individuals who were killed listed in the report. These are members of the army who were not engaged in the military activities but were taking food to a particular location on Sar Planina, so there were no combat activities and no need to act. So they were carrying food and there was a terrorist ambush and terrorist attack and murder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, in armed conflict, going back to our country X, isn't it common that members of one side attack and kill members of the other side?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In combat activity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can't people be attacked while they're eating their dinner? Is there a rule that says that they can't be attacked at dinner time, or breakfast time?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Turkish people did not kill people even at that time, but nowadays it is not so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move forward, please, to page 12 in the English version, and if we could go to page 12 in the Macedonian version as well, please. And in the Macedonian version, can we go forward one more page, please. Can we go forward one more page in the Macedonian version. And yet again, one more page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, in your version, towards the top of the page, there's an entry beginning with: "On 21/6/2001 ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Registrar, well, that's fine now.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's fine. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's at the bottom of the page in English. And we're told on June 21, 2001, around 1700 hours, from different positions in the lotion called Shipkovecki Bacila and in the village of Sipkovica terrorist groups attacked the Macedonian security forces at Popova Sapka. Seven grenades fell in this location but did not injure any of the policemen. As a response, our forces attacked the terrorist positions with artillery weapons and totally pushed them back." Was this a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was expecting to continue with the story about the previous event. You forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please do not, Dr. Markovski. I want you to answer the question that I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. I accept it. So in my opinion, this is not a terrorist group, that is to say, terrorist attack, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I forget, I would seek to tender this document now I believe it was 65 ter 701. Ms. Residovic is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document is already Exhibit 1D342, and there is no need to be admitted again as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn back to your expert report, Dr. Markovski, would you turn to paragraph 74, please. Actually, I think -- no, I will turn to paragraph 74 for a moment. At the beginning of your paragraph 74, you explain that, as a result of the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, the state organs, acting pursuant to Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, informed the United Nations Security Council and requested from the UN Security Council the undertaking of urgent activities by KFOR to strictly adhere to the regulations relating to the movement of military and paramilitary groups, arms shipment, movement restricts, and the gathering of large groups of individuals in the international zone ..." Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, Article 51, I think you know, falls under Chapter 7 of the United Nations Charter, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware what Article 51 of the Charter speaks about, about the right on collective an individual self-defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, we would move along more quickly if you would listen to my question and just respond to my question. My question was simply this Article 51 falls within Chapter 7 of the United Nations Charter, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it falls in chapter number 7. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Will you take my word for it for the purposes of this question?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reason why I shouldn't do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Thank you. Well, chapter 7 of the UN charter addresses actions with respect to threats to the peace, breaches of the peace and acts of aggression. And my question for you is this: Didn't the actions of the NLA, in 2001, fall within each of these three categories?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply I don't have an answer. I don't know. Let's analyse them one by one, and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, your answer is you don't know.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this particular moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, do you know whether -- well, given the subject matter of Chapter 7 of the UN Charter, action with respect to threats to the peace, breaches of the peace, and acts of aggression, do you know whether that was why the government of Macedonia felt that it was appropriate to invoke Article 51 of Chapter 7?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the government decided to invoke Article 51 of the UN Charter, but I know that to the Security Council of the United Nations, they asked for immediate activities by KFOR because it was obvious that the Republic of Macedonia was facing problems in providing the security of the national border between Kosovo and the Republic of Macedonia, because, basically, the border was secured only on the Macedonian side and for one or other reasons they would say that the border in depth of two kilometres towards Kosovo is mined by the former Yugoslav army when it was retreated, was retreating from this area and that is why they justified this decision not to provide security of the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us understanding is, though, Dr. Markovski, why do you say that you don't know whether the government decided to invoke Article 51 of the UN Charter, when in paragraph 74 of your report you say that: "As a result of the emerging crisis the state organs acts pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, informed the UN Security Council and made certain requests?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my position. I guessed that this is so, but I was not present at the governmental session in order to be sure. So this is why I said it. My assumption is that they refer to the right of collective an individual self-defence. So this paragraph, as can you see there are no quotation marks so this is my personal opinion and position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so what you say there in paragraph 74 the phrase "acting pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter," that's just your assumption, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, absolutely, because it is not in quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you think that's a very scientific way to draft your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? This is my conclusion from the result of their reaction. Because immediately afterward we had a reaction by the Security Council which referred to certain resolutions, and they made their position known. On the other hand, the United Nations reacted and they welcome the international efforts, the UNMIK as well, in order to deal with the potential threats and danger in the Republic of Macedonia, and, at the end, the Security Council adopted the resolution 1345 thus condemning the terrorist violence including terrorist activities on certain parts of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sufficient indication --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours. Would this be a good time to take the first break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, could you turn, please, again, back to your expert report, and could we look at paragraph 76, please. Do you have paragraph 76 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The last sentence of paragraph 76 says this: "The armed Albanian extremists do not possess any data on the number of wounded extremists, which also serves to demonstrate that they were unorganized and uncontrolled groups of armed thugs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How does the first point that you make demonstrate -- excuse me. How does that point that you make about lack of data on number of wounded extremists demonstrate that they were unorganised and uncontrolled groups of armed thugs? How does one point indicate the other?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I don't hear the interpretation into Macedonian. Yes, I hear it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. How does the point that -- the comment that you make about lack of data on number of wounded extremists demonstrate that they were unorganised and uncontrolled groups of armed thugs? How does one point illustrate the other point?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply. One organised military structure has a special respect towards the members of it who have lost their lives or were wounded when working on attaining the goals of that organisation. That would mean when performing the service there. The documents that are available and that I had reviewed, the members of the armed extremists in the Republic of Macedonia have made a table, a document, discussing 52 individuals who were killed on their side. This document, if we ran a more profound analysis we will see that the many data are missing on many persons. For instance, where were they born, when were they born, it is not known where some of them were killed and for some of them is not known where they were buried. A serious military institution would not permit this, since what we have here is their members and what we have here is a tradition that they all need to be buried following all procedures of military tradition. And another aspect is, another data on which I base my conclusion is they really don't have data on how many injured they had. And this is based on the statements available to me, coming from both Mr. Ali Ahmeti and Mr. Gzim Ostreni, who represent themselves as having the highest responsibility within this structure. They both assert that they don't have these data.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you shown the witness statement of Mr. Nazim Bushi, who talked about the numbers of wounded men that were in his brigade, the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is 114th Brigade, as Mr. Bushi says, I'm speaking about the overall structure that wishes to represent itself as the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But my question was simply this, so you were not shown the ICTY witness statement of Nazim Bushi, were you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but if it was there among the documents, have I seen it. But I'm not sure whether I have really seen it. I don't think I have analysed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how about the ICTY witness statement and I hope I'm pronouncing the name correctly. Rasim Haliti, who talked about the number of wounded persons in his brigade. Were you shown that statement?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are directing me only -- in a fragmentary fashion to certain groups, the organisation that wishes to represent itself as the National Liberation Army does not have any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just asking, sir, you can just answer yes or no, whether, prior to completing your report you reviewed the ICTY witness statement of Rasim Haliti.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen Rasim Haliti's, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you see what he said about the number of wounded men in his brigade?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is not the answer to the question how many wounded and killed were in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to move on. If you take a look at paragraph 77, the very next paragraph, Doctor. In the beginning of the paragraph you say: "The signing of the framework agreement in August 2001 as a political agreement between the relevant political subjects in the Republic of Macedonia and the presence of representatives from the European Union, NATO, and the United States of America, signalled the end of the hostilities ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By "hostilities," do you mean the end of the fighting between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Since, unfortunately, this document, signed by the relevant political structures in the Republic of Macedonia, failed to bring the peace ultimately. It did not relieve the situation of incidents an armed provocations. It continued and continued over the longer period of time. But this document was still a signal and a strong pressure from both the political structure, the relevant ones in the Republic of Macedonia but also from the international factor --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I need to stop you there. My question was something else. I'm interested in your use of the word "hostilities." And I want to know whether by the word "hostilities" you mean the end of fighting between the NLA and the security forces of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then how were you using the term "hostilities" in that sentence? What does "hostilities" mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the political sense, since the Ohrid Framework Agreement as a political agreement among the relevant political structures in the Republic of Macedonia, started the processes of further democratisation of the Macedonian society and created inequitable circumstances for absence of any hostilities amongst any political, economic, social, ethnic or other groups in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, wasn't the primary purpose of the Ohrid Agreement to stop the fighting?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary purpose of the Ohrid Framework Agreement was that there were no territorial solutions for any disputes in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after that, wasn't the next purpose to stop the fighting?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. At the end, the last sentence of paragraph 77 you're still talking about the Ohrid Agreement, and at the very end of that sentence you refer to the: "Decentralisation of a large number of the responsibilities on a municipal level?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you kindly repeat it, please? I apologise for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Take a look at the last sentence of paragraph 77.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And one of the things that the Ohrid Agreement did was it also provided for the decentralisation of certain Macedonian government institutions, such as the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's because in 2001 the Ministry of Internal Affairs was quite a centralised institution, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't give you a specific answer to this. With regards to the situation in the Ministry of Interior, I can't really speak about it. I don't know it well. But let's suppose it is like you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday, you recall from yesterday, I hope, and this is at pages 10735 to 10736 of the transcript, we looked together at the 1992 Law on Defence. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I asked you whether we saw that the 1992 law did not define the powers or duties of the General Staff, but you asked to see the 1995 law. Do you remember that discussion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, we now have the 1995 law available, and I would like to show it to you, please. I think we even have some hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be 65 ter 1D01215.2, and there contains some amendments to the Law on Defence which was passed in 1995. And if that can be called up on e-court, the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you take a look at this -- the decree to announce the law on changing the Law on Defence, it is published in the Official Gazette on June 7th, 1995. And you can see here, Dr. Markovski, that there are just five amendments to the Law on Defence, and these -- each amendment addresses amounts of money, and I believe they relate actually to fines that are imposed during disciplinary measures. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in the 1995 law or amendments to the law, there's -- we see nothing yet about the powers and responsibilities of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, even Gods are silent before the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would like to tender, first, what was the 1992 law that was discussed yesterday, and that is 65 ter 1236. And I would also like to tender this document, the 1995 amendments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received as two parts of the one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be exhibit number P00606.1 that's referring to 65 ter 1236. And 65 ter 1D01215.2 shall be P00606.2. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now do you also recall from our discussion yesterday, Dr. Markovski, that we looked at the 2001 Law on Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the parties that is 1D0098.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you remember when we looked through the 2001 law as well yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we started reviewing it, but then probably because of what you are showing here, we stopped it. Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are starting to agree a lot. It might not be well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think it's great, actually. And in the time that we spent on the 2001 law yesterday, we saw these provisions or amendments, if you will, that then specifically defined the roles and responsibilities of the General Staff of the army, right? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And you also described yesterday how, during the crisis time in 2001, the General Staff was fully functioning. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. All throughout the crisis, even before the crisis and after it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, so those amendments, first of all, the amendments to the 2001 law that addressed the roles and responsibilities of the General Staff, what those amendments did really was formalise a situation that already existed, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have very general. But let's analyse it, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But can you answer my question. Since the General Staff was functioning before June of 2001, then what those amendments did was formalise the position an operation of the General Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which amendments are you referring to? This is why I asked you. It is rather general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is 1D00098, please. And, Your Honours, this is at tab 48 and it's binder 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If binder 2 could be given to the witness, in case you'd like to look at this in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I wish you to understand what I'm asking, when we are discussing the law, I wish to have the law in front of me to see it. Otherwise I don't wish to obstruct you in your work, but this is why I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that's fine, that is perfectly fine. And I just need to find the right chapter. Turn to, please, what is chapter 4 and take a look at Article -- excuse me. Yeah, and take a look at Article 28 of the 2001 law. And Article 28 is in a subchapter called command in the armed forces. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the third paragraph says: "Immediate command with the armed forces is carried out by the chief of the General Staff as well as commanders of the military units ...." You see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And of the institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. One moment, please. Yes. If you take a look at Article 26. Article 26 says: "For the purposes of accomplishing the activities in Article 25, the General Staff of the army forces accomplishes the following ..." And then there's a list of responsibilities of the General Staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a total of 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. And then if you turn to Article 27, we see that the chief manages the General Staff of the armed forces who is appointed and discharged by the president. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is appointed and dismissed. The competencies for appointments and dismissal discharge of the chief of the General Staff belong to the president, to the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. But the point is Articles 26 and 27 they are new provisions in the Law on Defence and since the General Staff was already running all during the crisis you explain that General Petrovski was the chief of the General Staff. What we see here is that these Articles in the new law effectively formalise what had was an ongoing situation, right? Defined in law something that was already existing, already operating. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is very general but probably we will arrive at this conclusion of yours through the next questions. I will not give you a specific answer now because I can't. If you ask me a more specific question then I will really be able to answer it, but I expect next question, so let's see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, how about this? Article 26, subparagraph 8 says that: The General Staff of the armed forces will plan and organise and accomplish training activities for the armed forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is the document where you see it? In 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We were looking at the 2001 Law on Defence, Article 26, what we've been looking at for the last few minutes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're speaking about item 16 of Article 26?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, no. Let's speak about -- let's speak about item 3. Okay?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... supervises taking measures for the readiness of the armed forces and takes measures for their execution." Do you see that? Do you see that? Can you just say yes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, but is it what you said or what the interpreter said, the interpretation I receive differs substantial. I will try and read it in Macedonian and let the interpreters interpret it back to you because there is an important thing here. It is about the readiness of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe that we agree here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it organises and monitors carrying out of measures for readiness of the army and undertakes measures for their execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you understand, because readiness is something very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. But the bottom line is, even before the new law was passed in 2001, the General Staff was fulfilling this role that's described in Article 3, right? It was already doing this.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before passing the law of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what would it do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, there was a crisis time in --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I'm sorry. [Interpretation] no, no, I meant 1991, I apologise, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in 2001 the General Staff was performing some of these responsibilities that are laid out there Article 26, even before the new law was enacted, right? We need a verbal response.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So that means that these provisions or at least to some degree, were simply -- were codifying or formalising a situation that already existed, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I'm really making efforts, but I don't understand the question. Which situation is -- was codified? I don't know what you're asking of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The fact that the General Staff of the army of Republic of Macedonia, before June of 2001, was involved in organising and taking measures or monitoring of taking measures for the readiness of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And you also describe the yesterday how the General Staff was fully functioning in 2001. And so at least these parts of the 2001 Law on Defence, the parts that describe the work of the General Staff, they went into effect immediately, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was no reason for any delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please turn, if you can -- can you turn, please, to the end of this law. If you go all the way to Article 172?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Article 172 says: "Regulations issuing of which is foreseen by this law will be issued in a period of one year from the date it is put into effect." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Expect for Articles 142, 143, and 144 from chapter 12, which will be passed in a maximum of two years." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is what it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But Article 172 doesn't specifically define what parts of the law will require regulations and which parts will not, does it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Article does not specify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Could you turn back to your report, please. If we could take a look at paragraph 102 of your report. Paragraph 102 says that: "In view of the fact that the security forces were employed in conditions when a state of war or a state of emergency were not declared, the members of the reservist ranks of the army of Republic of Macedonia could have been called up for exercises or mobilisation exercises." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it reads, and this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, but in reality, weren't the army reservists who were called up in 2001 called up for much more than just exercises. They were also called up to fight the members of the NLA, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the invitations, one could read that they're being called up for an exercise or mobilisation exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But during the crisis time in 2001, once these reservists were called up, some of them, at least, found themselves in positions where they were actually fighting the NLA. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within these 30 days while the exercise lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, so in 2001, the Law on Defence, if I can use an American expression I hope it will translate all right in your language. The Law on Defence was bent just a little bit to provide the army with the manpower that it needed. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The law is fine, and the law provides for all other possibilities for mobilisation or use of the army. If you pose this as a problem, as an issue, it should refer to the declaration or non-declaration of state of war so this is what is important for any further legislation and implementation of the provisions of the Defence law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But would you not include fighting within the definition of an exercise, a military exercise, would you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn, please, to paragraph 148 in your expert report, the last sentence of paragraph 148 says this: "Nevertheless estimates show that the army had a total of approximately 8.000 personnel at its disposal, of which only approximately 3.000 were directly involved in the protection of the territory under their control, not including the personnel from the border brigade." Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You use the phrase here "under their control," because during the crisis time part of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia was under the control of the NLA. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such thing in my sentence. Let's try it again. Following the same system we applied earlier. It was rather efficient. I will read the sentence and then it will be interpreted into English for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "However, the estimates speak that the army, on a monthly level, disposed of, in total, around 8.000 personnel, out of which 3.000 were directly engaged for the protection of the territory of their responsibility or under their responsibility, excluding the personnel of the border brigade, which provided security at the border."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the English translation that was provided to us by Defence counsel has the phrase "under their control," so that's why I asked you that question. But thank you for clarifying that. If you could take a look at paragraph 149, just the next paragraph. At the start of paragraph 149, towards the end of the initial paragraph, you're referring to the combat actions of the army, and you say: "They only undertook active combat actions on five or six occasions ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what happened and this is how it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you list five or six -- you list, I believe, six, actually, examples --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I list six examples, because five of them were implemented. That's why I say five to six. Out of the six issued orders by the Supreme Corps Commander, five were implemented. One was not implemented by the General Staff, and that is why the Chief of Staff was discharged on the 9th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So just so that I understand your testimony, these six occasions that you're referring to, you're referring to six occasions where the Supreme Commander gave an order to the army, to undertake combat activity. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So, for example, your six examples here would not include the fighting around Radusa that we saw earlier this morning, in the video-clip, from the 11th of August. That wouldn't be included within these six examples, would it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But one has to bear in mind that I'm discussing here, and I am very specific that in five cases only, active combat activities have been carried out. That is to say, operations that have been organised and planned by the security bodies of the Republic of Macedonia. Radusa is not an action organised and planned by the security structures of the Republic of Macedonia. Radusa was a situation when armed extremists groups attacked the police station and the members of the police, later on, in the afternoon hours, and with the support of army structures, found themselves in a situation where they were defending themselves. So they did not undertake active combat activities. This would mean attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
